messages.content: Spokane update: the Thursday training is now 7:30 a.m. because two operators can only come first thing. So Thursday same-day travel is out. Can you redo the Wednesday flight choice and the hotel trade-off? I also need a plan for the 45-pound demo case.

Agreed, I would not try Thursday morning travel with a 7:30 start. The earlier 1:10 United nonstop from the placeholder is not pricing well now, so the practical Wednesday choices are: safer outbound, Alaska SFO-SEA-GEG 12:20 p.m.-5:03 p.m. with a 1 hour 22 minute Seattle connection; later nonstop, United SFO-GEG 5:15 p.m.-7:28 p.m. The nonstop is simpler in the air, but it puts hotel arrival around 8:15 or later before dinner. The Alaska connection is the better fit for protecting Thursday.
I do not love adding the connection. Is Seattle enough cushion or is that a trap?

It is workable. The connection is on one carrier, bags check through, and 1:22 at Seattle is not a sprint. It is not as clean as nonstop, but the trade-off is that you are in Spokane early enough to absorb a modest delay. The late nonstop has no transfer risk but gives you almost no evening buffer.
Use SFO unless Oakland is clearly better. Now compare the hotels again.

For the earlier start, Spokane Valley wins on logistics. Mirabeau Park in Spokane Valley is about 10-12 minutes from the distributor warehouse, has free parking, guest feedback around 4.3, and Max at Mirabeau on site. Downtown Davenport Grand is better reviewed, around 4.6, and has much better restaurant density, but the morning drive is more like 25-30 minutes and parking is less convenient. Downtown is the comfort pick; Valley is the schedule pick.
Valley is fine, but I do not want to be stuck with vending machine dinner.

Mirabeau is the better Valley choice for that reason. It has the on-site restaurant, and there are a few Spokane Valley Mall and Sullivan Road dinner options within a short drive. The other Valley hotels closer to the warehouse are thinner for food.
Okay, pencil in Mirabeau, not downtown. What do we do with the demo case?

Best handling is to ship it straight to the distributor warehouse if they can receive and lock it overnight. Backup is hotel delivery, but I would only do that if Mirabeau confirms they accept a 45-pound case and whether any storage fee applies. Checking it on the flight is the least attractive option because it adds airport handling and rental-car hassle.
I will ask the distributor for a receiving contact and dock hours. If they say yes, the hotel should not be involved.
Marked that way: distributor receiving is the primary plan, hotel package acceptance is backup only. I would wait to book until that answer and the Friday timing are both confirmed.
Friday may include a partner check after lunch, but they are saying it should not go past 1. Is the 2:25 nonstop return still too tight?

If you are done by noon, the 2:25 GEG-SFO nonstop is fine. If it truly runs to 1, it is tight unless the case stays with the distributor and you are traveling light. Acceptable backup is the 4:05 p.m. Alaska return via Seattle. Ask them whether the partner check ends by noon and whether they keep the case; then book 2:25 if noon is firm, 4:05 if not.

Do not ship to the hotel.

messages.content: New trip: Hampton Roads water authority wants me there for a Tuesday noon pre-walk and a Wednesday 6:30 a.m. plant access window. They may add a Thursday operator session. I need Bay Area flights and a hotel shortlist. Norfolk versus Richmond is fair game.
I can work that up. What dates are these, and do you want to travel Monday rather than Sunday?
Pre-walk is Tuesday March 10, plant access Wednesday March 11. Travel Monday March 9 if possible. No red-eye. Reliable arrival matters more than airline. One connection is okay; no two-stop mess.

Understood. I will compare ORF and RIC with a Monday arrival, avoid two-stop itineraries, and keep the return flexible until the Thursday session is confirmed. Are you planning to drive yourself from the airport to the plant area?
Yes, rental car. If there is no Thursday session, I could leave Thursday morning. If there is one, probably Thursday afternoon unless they push it late.

Flight shortlist: best fit into Norfolk is Delta SFO-ATL-ORF on Monday, 9:45 a.m.-8:02 p.m., with a 1 hour 31 minute Atlanta connection. Backup is United SFO-IAD-ORF, 10:30 a.m.-9:18 p.m., with a shorter IAD connection. American via Charlotte is similar but the connection is tighter. Richmond is cheaper on some fares, but by the time you add the drive, you reach the hotel later than ORF.
Anything closer to noon departure that does not land ridiculously late?

The noon-ish departures into ORF mostly arrive between 10:45 p.m. and midnight. The least bad is United SFO-IAD-ORF around 12:35 p.m.-10:58 p.m. with a reasonable connection, but it leaves little room for delay, dinner, or a rental-car issue. For this one, late morning is safer.
Okay. Hotels should be on the right side for the plant, not downtown Norfolk unless it is clearly better. I need parking and some place to eat nearby.

Assuming the plant is on the Suffolk/Harbour View side, I would start with these: Hilton Garden Inn Chesapeake/Suffolk Harbour View, about 15-20 minutes to the plant area, free parking, on-site restaurant, and several nearby casual restaurants. Hyatt Place Chesapeake/Greenbrier, more dining around it and free parking, but more like 25-30 minutes to the plant. Norfolk Waterside Marriott has the best downtown dining, but paid parking and a longer drive, so I would not lead with it for a 6:30 gate time.
The address is in Suffolk near Harbour View. Restaurant onsite is useful, but not if the drive gets bad.

Then the Harbour View option is the better fit. Hilton Garden Inn keeps the morning drive short and gives you an on-site dinner option. Hyatt Place Greenbrier is the acceptable backup if the rate or cancellation terms are better, but it buys food choice at the cost of a longer morning.
Check ratings and room basics. I do not want a 3.6 place because it is close.

I would drop anything in that range. The Hilton Garden Inn Chesapeake/Suffolk is showing around 4.1 on guest-facing ratings, Hyatt Place Greenbrier around 4.2, and Courtyard Suffolk Chesapeake around 4.0. HGI and Hyatt list mini-fridge and coffee maker in the rooms; Courtyard lists mini-fridge, with coffee maker dependent on room type, so that one needs confirmation.
What does Richmond actually save?

Current Richmond fares are about $120-$180 lower than ORF, but RIC adds roughly 90 minutes of driving after the flight and more exposure to traffic. The rental car cost is similar. I would only use Richmond if ORF fares jump or the ORF connections deteriorate.
Use ORF then. How would you handle the unknown Thursday session?

I would hold the hotel as March 9-12, checking out Thursday. That covers Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday nights without forcing a Wednesday-night flight after the plant day. For flights, keep two return branches: if no Thursday session, ORF-ATL-SFO Thursday morning around 7:00 a.m.-12:20 p.m.; if the operator session happens, ORF-ATL-SFO Thursday 2:15 p.m.-7:05 p.m. If they push late Thursday, add one hotel night and return Friday.
Client says they will confirm by Friday. Mark the best and backup, but do not book yet.

Marked, no booking. Best fit: Delta SFO-ATL-ORF Mon Mar. 9, 9:45 a.m.-8:02 p.m.; rental car at ORF; Hilton Garden Inn Chesapeake/Suffolk Harbour View Mar. 9-12; return depends on the Friday answer. Backup: United via IAD into ORF if the Delta fare moves, and Hyatt Place Greenbrier if the HGI cancellation terms are worse.
If there is no Thursday session, I would rather fly Thursday morning than drag through Atlanta Wednesday night.

Noted. The working plan now assumes ORF, a Harbour View/Suffolk-area hotel, and no Wednesday-night return. Return branch one is Thursday morning if work ends Wednesday; branch two is Thursday mid-afternoon if they add the operator session; branch three is Friday only if Thursday runs late. I will wait for the client’s Friday confirmation before booking.
